title: Applying organization: what goes where
blurb: Apply the organization practice in a scenario: the right product for each arrangement, structures for one or many teams, and the skill matrix, delegation poker and delegation matrix.
question: At Callowmere University, wellbeing staff work across two campuses and some work remotely. The project manager wants to set out sync co-location days and the online tools teams will use for transparency. Where should this be recorded?

teach.h: Organization: the 'who' of an agile project
teach.body: The organization practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities. PRINCE2 Agile keeps the governance roles and the project manager, then adds agile roles at delivery level: a product owner, team coach, developers and testers for each team. An agile coach supports the organization's adoption of agile. Three management products and three techniques make the structure work.

teach.h: Layers of the agile project structure

levels.label: Governance roles
levels.sub: Project executive, CPO, senior supplier; project assurance

levels.label: Project manager
levels.sub: Supported by project support; advised by the agile coach

levels.label: Product owner per team
levels.sub: A version of the team manager role

levels.label: Delivery team
levels.sub: Developers and testers, with a team coach

teach.caption: The PM is the only role with direct authority over the PO; the PO is the only role with direct authority over delivery team members (7.3.1).

head: Product
Holds
Example
rows: Procurement and contract form that supports agile
Fixed team cost per iteration, MVP, agreed DoD
Who is involved, relationships, working practices
Co-location days, remote tools, performance reviews
The PM will be mentored by the agile coach
teach.caption: Structure content: structure chart, summary of authority and responsibilities, working practices and arrangements, supporting information.

teach.h: How work flows down the structure
teach.body: The project manager agrees work with each product owner as a work package description, which in agile is a set of user stories, within tolerances and the management approaches. The PO delivers it within those limits and owns the team's product backlog. The CPO keeps the project backlog aligned with the team backlogs and settles priorities between teams.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Larkspur Rail, three teams
teach.body: Project manager Rhys Pengelly sorts the arrangements. How Coinbridge's fixed-price contract will still support agile delivery (an MVP definition, tolerances, an agreed DoD) goes in the commercial management approach. Remote working with Coinbridge and the shared tools go in the project management team structure. 'Rhys will be mentored by the agile coach' goes in the role descriptions. Matteo Ricci, as CPO, sets priorities across all three teams; each team has its own PO. At kickoff each team completes a skill matrix and a delegation matrix.

teach.text: Near misses: co-location and remote arrangements, system access and performance reviews are working practices in the project management team structure, not role descriptions. The commercial management approach covers selecting and contracting suppliers, not the supplier's own daily agile practices. The CPO prioritizes across teams; a PO owns one team's backlog.

items: Commercial approach: contract form that supports agile (cost per iteration, MVP, DoD).
Team structure: who, relationships, working practices, co-location and remote arrangements.
Role descriptions: specific responsibilities, such as the PM being mentored by the agile coach.
Many teams: one PM, one CPO across teams, a PO per team, team coaches for one or two teams.
Skill matrix (kickoff, team dashboard); delegation poker (agree); delegation matrix (show).

summary: You can now place an organization arrangement in the right product, set up the structure for one or several teams, and choose between the skill matrix, delegation poker and delegation matrix. You can also follow the lines of authority from PM to PO to team.

A.q: Callowmere University pays Northmere Systems for each two-week iteration. The project manager wants the agreement to include a definition of the MVP, tolerances and an agreed Definition of Done. Where should the form of contract that supports agile delivery be described?
A.why: The commercial management approach sets out the procurement and contract form so that it supports agile, for example fixed teams or costs per iteration, an MVP definition and tolerances, and an agreed DoD (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: The team structure covers who is involved and how they work together, not the contract form.
whyNot.1: Role descriptions set out each role's responsibilities, not contract terms.
whyNot.3: The benefits management approach covers benefits actions and reviews (business case practice).

A.q: Callowmere's wellbeing staff work across two campuses, and some work part-time or remotely. The project manager wants to set out sync co-location days and the online tools that teams will use for transparency and rich communication. Where should this be recorded?
A.why: The project management team structure describes who is involved, their relationships and how they work together, including arrangements for co-location or remote teams and the tools for transparency and rich communication (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions cover specific responsibilities of roles, not working arrangements.
whyNot.2: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts.
whyNot.3: The skill matrix maps capabilities and gaps, not working arrangements.

A.q: Easterholm County Council is bringing in Gita Bhatt as agile coach for six months. It wants it recorded that she will mentor project manager Simon Archer, who is new to agile. Where should this be recorded?
A.why: Role descriptions set out the roles in the project management team and their specific responsibilities, such as the PM being mentored by the agile coach (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: The team structure shows who is involved and how they work together, not one role's specific duty.
whyNot.1: The commercial approach covers how her services are procured, not what her role involves.
whyNot.2: A delegation matrix shows who decides what per decision area, not a mentoring responsibility.

B.q: At Pinewick, the e-commerce team and the store operations team each have a product owner. Customer messages about click and collect must be consistent, and the teams disagree about which stores' features come first. Which role should set the priorities across both teams?
B.why: The CPO represents the users, owns the project backlog and makes sure priorities are clearly defined across teams (Table 7.2, Figure 7.2).

whyNot.1: A PO owns one team's product backlog and does not prioritize across teams.
whyNot.2: The PM is a servant leader linking governance and teams; prioritizing across teams is not the PM's role.
whyNot.3: The agile coach removes organization-level blockers; prioritizing user stories is not an agile coach task.

B.q: Draycott's maintenance engineers and software team keep arguing about who may change alert thresholds and who must be consulted. The project manager wants a visible record of who decides and who is involved for each decision area. Which technique should be used?
B.why: A delegation matrix makes responsibilities and decision-making authority transparent, showing who decides and who is involved per decision area (7.4.3).

whyNot.0: A skill matrix shows capabilities and gaps, not decision rights.
whyNot.1: Delegation poker is the collaborative technique for agreeing decision-making; the visible record per area is the matrix.
whyNot.2: The project dashboard shows release status, burn charts, risks and issues, not decision rights.

B.q: In Saltmarsh's project kickoff workshop, the service design team wants to map who can run testing sessions with older tenants, who needs portal training and where skills overlap. Which technique should it use?
B.why: The team skill matrix gives an overview of capabilities, strengths, gaps and training needs; it is completed collaboratively in the project kickoff workshop and shown on the team dashboard (7.4.1, Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The delegation matrix shows decision authority, not skills.
whyNot.2: Role descriptions set out responsibilities of roles, not individual skills and gaps.
whyNot.3: Delegation poker agrees decision-making levels, not skills.

C.q: Larkspur Rail has three delivery teams, including one from Coinbridge Payments. The project manager proposes appointing a second project manager to run the Coinbridge team. Is this an appropriate application of the organization practice, and why?
options: Yes, because every delivery team needs its own manager
Yes, because Coinbridge works under a fixed-price contract
No, because a multi-team project keeps one project manager
No, because the senior supplier runs supplier delivery teams
C.why: With several teams there is still one project manager; each team has its own product owner, and the CPO sets priorities across teams (7.3.1, Figure 7.2).

whyNot.0: Each team's day-to-day lead is its product owner, a version of the team manager, not another PM.
whyNot.1: The contract type does not change the structure; the commercial approach handles the contract.
whyNot.3: The senior supplier represents the supplier side at governance level; the PO leads the team day to day.

C.q: Easterholm's agreement with Abacus Care Software uses fixed-price change requests that take six weeks to quote. The project manager proposes a fixed team cost per iteration with an agreed Definition of Done, recorded in the commercial management approach. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because the contract form should support agile delivery
Yes, because it lets the cost flex with the scope delivered
No, because contract terms belong in the team structure
No, because the senior supplier sets the contract terms
C.why: The commercial management approach should make the procurement and contract form support agile development, for example fixed delivery teams or costs per iteration and an agreed DoD (Table 7.3).

whyNot.1: Cost is fixed with zero tolerance; a fixed cost per iteration keeps cost fixed while scope flexes.
whyNot.2: The team structure covers people, relationships and working practices, not contract terms.
whyNot.3: The management approaches, including the commercial approach, are agreed in initiation and approved by the project executive; the senior supplier does not set them.

C.q: Before Saltmarsh's kickoff workshop, the project manager writes a delegation matrix for the service design team and issues it, without discussion, to save workshop time. Is this an appropriate application of the organization practice, and why?
options: Yes, because a delegation matrix makes authority transparent
Yes, because the project manager directs the team members
No, because decision rights belong in the commercial approach
No, because delegation should be agreed with the team itself
C.why: Decision-making within teams is defined collaboratively (delegation poker, 7.4.2), and the kickoff's team delegation matrix topic aims to empower self-management. Issuing it without the team defeats that purpose.

whyNot.0: True of a delegation matrix, but it does not explain whether imposing one is effective.
whyNot.1: The PM's direct authority is over the PO; the PO has authority over team members (7.3.1).
whyNot.2: The commercial approach covers procurement and contracts, not team decision rights.

reteach.title: A restaurant kitchen
reteach.question: In a busy restaurant, where would you write down the supplier deal, the rota, each chef's duties and who may change the menu?

blocks.body: The deal with the fish supplier is the commercial management approach. The rota, who works which station and how the kitchen communicates is the project management team structure. Each chef's job card is a role description. The board showing who can cook what is the skill matrix, and the sheet showing who may change the menu is the delegation matrix. One head chef runs the kitchen, just as one project manager runs a multi-team project.

blocks.text: Remote and co-location arrangements are working practices (team structure), not a role duty.

explain.body: Commercial management approach: contract and procurement form. Project management team structure: who, relationships, working practices and arrangements. Role descriptions: each role's specific responsibilities.

test.q: Draycott is adding a contract data scientist to Hannah Reece's work. The project manager wants to record that she will need access to the factory network and will have a performance review at each stage end. Where should this go?
test.why: Performance reviews and access to systems are working practices and arrangements, part of the project management team structure (Table 7.3).

whyNot.0: Role descriptions hold responsibilities, not system access or review arrangements.
whyNot.1: The commercial approach covers how she is procured, not her working arrangements.
whyNot.3: The skill matrix maps capabilities and gaps.

explain.body: One project manager; one CPO prioritizing across teams; a product owner for each team; team coaches working with one or two teams; every team has the same composition as a single-team project.

test.q: Which structure fits Larkspur Rail's three delivery teams?
options: One PM, one CPO, a PO for each team
Three PMs, one CPO, one PO
One PM, one PO, three team coaches
One PM, three CPOs, one PO
test.why: A multi-team project keeps one PM and one CPO, with a product owner for each team (Figure 7.2).

whyNot.1: There is one project manager, and each team needs its own PO.
whyNot.2: Each team needs its own PO; one PO cannot own three team backlogs.
whyNot.3: One CPO sets priorities across teams; the POs are per team.

explain.body: The PM is the only role with direct authority over the PO. The PO, a version of the team manager role, is the only role with direct authority over delivery team members. Work is agreed PM to PO as sets of user stories.

test.q: At Callowmere University, who has direct authority over the developers in the web team?
test.why: The product owner is the only role with direct authority over delivery team members (7.3.1).

whyNot.0: The PM's direct authority is over the PO, not the team members.
whyNot.2: The team coach helps the team self-manage; it has no line authority.
whyNot.3: The CPO prioritizes across teams; it does not direct team members.

explain.body: Delegation poker is a collaborative technique for defining decision-making within teams. The delegation matrix then makes the result transparent: who decides and who is involved per decision area.

test.q: Easterholm's digital team and the social workers who join it want to agree together, using cards, how much freedom the team has over screen design decisions. Which technique are they using?
test.why: Delegation poker is the collaborative technique for defining decision-making within teams (7.4.2).

whyNot.0: The skill matrix maps capabilities, not decision freedom.
whyNot.1: The matrix records the outcome per decision area; agreeing it together with cards is delegation poker.
whyNot.3: Role descriptions are a management product, not a collaborative technique.
